sentences.text: They are heard.
Perused the case diary/challan papers.

2. This is the applicant's first application under Section 483 of Bhartiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita,
2023 (Section 439 of Criminal Procedure Code, 1973), as they are implicated in connection with Crime No.500/2024 registered at Police Station - Aerodrome, Indore (MP) for offence punishable under Sections 409, 420, 34, 467, 468, 471 of IPC.
The applicant Rajesh is in custody since 2.12.2025 and applicant Sovan is in custody since 16.10.2025.
3. Allegation against the applicants is of committing fraud.
It is alleged that in the name of developing residential colony the applicants, who are real brothers, obtained about Rs.29 Lakhs from nine persons.

4. Counsel for the applicants, at the outset, has submitted that the NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-IND:8446 2 MCRC-11529-2026 applicants are ready to deposit aforesaid amount in the trial Court, however some breathing time may be given.
It is further submitted that the charge sheet has already been filed, applicants are in jail since 2.12.2025 & 16.10.2025 and the final conclusion of trial is likely to take sufficient long time.
Hence, it is submitted that the bail application be allowed and applicants be released on bail.

sentences.text: 5. Counsel for the State as well as objector have opposed the prayer and it is submitted that no case for grant of bail is made out.

6. Having considered the rival submissions and on perusal of the case diary and also the undertaking given by counsel for the applicants that the applicants are ready to deposit the aforesaid amount in the trial Court, this Court is inclined to allow the application.

7. Accordingly, without commenting upon the merits of the case, the application filed under Section 483 of the BNSS on behalf of the applicants is hereby allowed, subject to deposit of total sum o f Rs.29 Lakhs by the applicants or any other person on their behalf, out of which, Rs.5,00,000/-
(Rupees Five Lakhs) upfront before their release i.e. at the time of furnishing the bail bond in a fixed deposit in a nationalized bank and producing the receipt/certificate of the same before the concerned trial Court and rest of Rs.24,00,000/-(Rupees Twenty Four Lakhs) to be deposited by the applicants in 12 equal instalments of Rs.2,00,000/-(Rupees Two Lakhs only) each within a period of 12 months from the date of their release in a fix deposit in a nationalized bank and producing the receipt/certificate of the same before the concerned trial Court and the said amount shall be subject to NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:8446 3 MCRC-11529-2026 the final outcome of the case by the trial Court.

The deposit receipt/certificate so produced by the applicants shall be endorsed by the learned Judge of the lower Court to be, 'furnished towards the bail of the applicants and shall be subject to the final decision of the case by the trial Court'.
8.

It is further directed that the applicants-Rajesh and Sovan shall be released on bail on their furnishing a bond in the sum of Rs.25,000/- (Rupees Twenty five Thousand only) each with one solvent surety each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, to appear before the trial Court on the dates given by the Court.
This bail order shall be subject to furnishing an undertaking that the applicants will deposit the amount, respectively, as directed above.

It is also directed that the applicants will abide by all the conditions enumerated under Section 437(3) of the Cr.P.C.
9.

However, it is directed that if the applicants are found to be involved in violation of any of the terms of this order, an application for cancellation of his bail may be filed before the trial Court itself, which shall decide the same in accordance with law.
10. M.Cr.C. stands allowed and disposed of.

(SUBODH ABHYANKAR) JUDGE trilok Rajesh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 31 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/28426398/
